questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always thought that Milan is an interesting City and i would love to go to Italy. I have been to Rome once and the culture seemed nice. I found that the University of Milan had a lot of exciting classes.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the meaning in Copenhagen before arrival was very meaningful and it gave me a lot of insights that i found very usefull. Furthermore i think that there is a lot of practical things that you have to be aware of, but we were guided very much and that was very nice.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I followed the instructions given by the emails i recieved.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We knew someone from our own University in Copenhagen that knew someone who had been living in an apartment in Milan and we got their number through them. The owners were very kind and helpfull.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live with someone, so you can explore the city together and help each other through the whole period.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very time consuming and a litlte bit complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The emails i recieved was very helpfull and they replies were fast, so that was a big help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Overall succesfull i think. A first i registred to a class that i did not find that interesting, but then registered for another and that was quite easy and not a complicated process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: use time and be aware that you can easily shift class. Dont be scared that you have to take the exact classes that you registred for at the beginning.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i think both levels of the course was good. I could keep up with the MA classes even though i am on my BA myself.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite different, which was also what i found very interesting about beeing abroad. The way they teach and do things is different from at UCPH and especially the way they handle the exams was different than what i am used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled to the courses: Global Social dynamics, Languages of the media, Digital Society and Globalization and Cultural Diversity.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think that all the courses i had was very interesting, but but i would recommend Languages of the media and Digital Society especially..

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The extra insurance costs, but i think that depends on the insurance- company you use.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffe and food in general was very cheap and that was nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of social arrangements though the Erasmus organisation, but i dont really know what activities that were available at the institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go see a lot of the cultural buildings in the city and I would also reccomend to take day-trips around in italy to see more of the country. Como-lake f.eks.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Have fun and say YES to things. Take daytrips and make a lot of friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: i think it was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes and attend to some of the activites that are arranged for you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that much-

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The coffee and the food was amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
take som classes that you find interesting 
make a lot of new freinds
attend to the classes that you signed up for

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go there a few days before the school starts and take a look around the institution, so you know where it is and where to go when school starts. We did that, and that was very nice.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: A made a lot of new friends both from DK and from other places. Saw an other culture and had a lot of great experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: i missed home a bit and that was a challenge, but that was only for a couple days. I also think it is a good idea to start to look for appartments many months before you have to go, since i heard that some of my friends had a tough time finding somewhere to live.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Take care of you belongings. My bag was stolen.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
